name: TX-08
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district (R+13 PVI) with no Democratic fundraising presence
Steinmann raised over $2 million with outside support; Jones raised under $25,000
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
Open seat removes incumbency but not the partisan lean
model.rationale: The R+13 district, Steinmann's overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing a Republican win near 95% all point the same way, and no polling or ratings suggest movement toward Jones. The open seat adds some uncertainty, keeping this at Likely rather than Safe R.
model.watch: Any sign of Democratic fundraising or polling traction in this suburban Houston seat would warrant a shift, but none is currently visible.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Morgan Luttrell's retirement leaves this heavily Republican Houston-area seat open, but the district's R+13 lean makes it a steep climb for any Democrat. Republican Jessica Hart Steinmann enters the general election with more than $2 million raised and outside support, while Democrat Laura Jones has raised under $25,000 with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Republican win at roughly 95%. The open-seat dynamic adds modest uncertainty, but the evidence points clearly toward the GOP holding the seat.
